triethylammoniuim bicarbonate (TEA) solution in electropspray mass spectrometric analysis of macromolecules and noncovalent assemblies of macromolecules is a very efficient method that improves the separation of ions of close masses and that multiply charged ions generated under these conditions are significantly more stable in the gas phase.
the use of triethyl ammonium bicarbonate solution in electrospraying mass spectrometry is a very efficient way of studying proteins or non-covalent protein complexes in the gas phase.

the use of TEAB solution for electrospray mass spectral analysis of noncovalent biomolecular complexes results in the following: (a) the stabilization of gas-phase non-covalent complexes; (b) the generation of multiply charged ions that are easier to separate; (c) the generation of ions with a lower charge state, which improves the separation of ions of close masses.
